description: We are a team of ECE students passionate about space exploration, science communication, research, and creative storytelling. Our project explores the stories behind abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars through an engaging comic-style narrative. We welcome enthusiastic members with skills in research, illustration, graphic design, storytelling, content writing, and space science who are excited to turn ideas into reality!
summary:
Project Summary: Abandoned, But Not Forgotten

Space exploration leaves behind more than discoveries. It also leaves scientific instruments, spacecraft components and equipment on the surfaces of the Moon and Mars. Although these objects may no longer be operational, they represent important milestones in humanity's journey into space. However, their contributions and stories often remain overlooked.
Abandoned, But Not Forgotten is a proposed educational digital comic book that aims to bring these forgotten objects to life through creative storytelling. The project transforms real space equipment into fictional characters, allowing them to narrate their missions, purposes and experiences through engaging comic-style conversations and illustrations.
Beginning with the Apollo 11 mission, the comic explores equipment such as the Early Apollo Surface Experiments Package (EASEP) and the Lunar Module descent stage. It then extends to Mars, highlighting components of NASA's Perseverance landing system, including the heat shield, backshell, parachute and descent stage.
The stories will be developed using authentic NASA archives, mission records and scientific information, ensuring that creative narratives remain grounded in historical facts.
Our objective is to make space exploration history more accessible and engaging for students and the general public while encouraging curiosity about science, technology and engineering.
details: Abandoned, But Not Forgotten is an educational digital comic book that brings attention to scientific equipment and spacecraft components left behind on the Moon and Mars. It transforms these objects into fictional characters that share their stories through creative conversations and illustrations. Using NASA's official archives and mission records, the project explores equipment from the Apollo 11 mission and landing components of the Perseverance rover mission on Mars. It combines factual research with imaginative storytelling to make space science more engaging and accessible to students and the general public. We use NASA resources for research and digital design tools to develop the comic. Our team focuses on creativity, scientific accuracy, visual appeal and educational value. The project aims to inspire curiosity about space exploration and remind people that even after their missions end, these objects remain part of humanity's achievements.
